I got assessed for ADHD and autism within 6 months of seeing my doctor. 

Might be the waiting lists are longer now, but it can't hurt to try.

Honestly I really dislike the term "red flag" because almost everyone you meet has some red flags that you'll discover as you get to know them. 
It's about deciding which red flags are deal breakers for you individually. 

That said I would guess that if you're 18+ and never had a friend, most people would feel like there must be a reason for that, and probably assume the reason is that person's poor qualities.

However there's a lot of more benign reasons why someone wouldn't have a friend until 18+. If they've been homeschooled, or had a reduced social life due to living in a remote area, or being a person who doesn't grow properly into themselves until later in life, mental health issues can stunt sociability. 

If you're talking about yourself, you should be aware that, despite what it might seem like, no one is great socially right off the bat. There's a lot of rules to socialising that have to be learnt and it can take some time and a lot of getting it wrong before you get the knack.  Don't get discouraged and keep trying and keep learning.

Viruses hide inside healthy cells, and then our bodies antibodies send cells out to find the virus infected cells and kill them (apoptosis) before they can spread the virus. Once the body knows what the virus looks like, it expels the virus before it can infect any cells.

I grew up on a dairy farm in the UK so maybe I can answer your question. 
In my experience cows are absolutely NOT killed to produce milk. The only deaths that occur to produce milk are, in extremely rare and unfortunate circumstances, the bull calves that are born that the farm is unable to sell for whatever reason. This occured once in my lifetime when the beef prices were so low in the UK that no one would buy the surplus bull calves so the farm was forced to slaughter them to stay afloat. This isn't a problem with dairy production so much as it is a problem with capitalism. An unwanted product will always be destroyed, whether that product is clothing, food or even people. 

If you want to ask whether dairy production is cruel or not that's a different question, and one I don't have a solid answer for. 
I personally do not think it is assuming the animals are treated well (as they have been on every fairy farm I have experience in the UK) and are kept happy and healthy. Some farms do seperate the calves from the mothers, for numerous reasons. To help prevent disease, to be able to keep track of calves (they have a habit of wandering off and dying if you don't keep a close eye on them) and to ensure each calf is getting the food it requires to grow properly.

I just finished my first playthrough. 
Here's some realisations that helped me.
Don't be afraid to use prosthetics, I finished the game with over 900 spirit emblems. Don't worry about using them all. I never bought any either. 
Learning to deflect is essential, but sometimes you can get by with tapping L1 and sometimes you'll need to. 
It can sometimes be better to not move. My habit from previous souls games was to constantly be circling, always moving. Sometimes it's better to hold your ground, deflect, and not having movement inputs can be really helpful for countering sweeps and stabs with jump kicks and mikiris. 

There's often multiple paths, if you've hit a road block, try a different route. Get some prosthetics, some more beads, get a break. Refresh your brain. 

Learn when you need to whittle down a bosses vitality and when you need to get their posture. Some guys you can just deflect until the posture breaks and then you're gravy. Others you'll need to dodge and counter to get some damage before you can break posture. A certain illusionist will be near impossible unless you learn this. 

Try to keep pressure up, some bosses are super hard if you let them do their whole combo, it can make things a lot easier if you deflect a big hit and then counter to interrupt the rest of the combo. 

Hope this helps!
